items.title: Claude Meetings lets Anthropic's AI join your video calls
items.summary: Anthropic is adding Claude directly to video calls. Claude Meetings joins Google Meet sessions and creates documents, whiteboards, and meeting notes in real time. The feature launches in beta for Team and Enterprise plans, with more platforms coming later. The article Claude Meetings lets Anthropic's AI join your video calls appeared first on The Decoder.

items.title: Google's Gemini 4 Hydrogen outscores the bigger Argon just four weeks after its launch
items.summary: Google's Gemini 4 Hydrogen replaces the Flash series, but benchmarks suggest it also makes the pricier Argon obsolete. On the independent Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, Hydrogen nearly matches Claude Sonnet 5.5 for less money but costs about 2.5 times more per task than GPT-6.1 Sol and still falls short on agentic coding. items.title: OpenAI’s data suggests that frontier models are hiding their thoughts because developers optimize for capability and compute
items.summary: OpenAI's safety team systematically investigated why the chains of thought in frontier models like GPT-6 Astra are increasingly evading oversight. Four training steps drive the erosion, including architecture choices and reinforcement learning. The analysis shows that the loss of transparency is not a law of nature but also reflects tradeoffs around capability and cost. items.title: ElevenLabs Scribe v3 Live uses conversational context to stop voice agents from cutting off callers mid-sentence
items.summary: ElevenLabs has released Scribe v3 and Scribe v3 Live, two new speech recognition models designed to transcribe accurately through background noise and crosstalk. Benchmarks from Artificial Analysis confirm that Scribe v3 narrowly beats competitors like OpenAI, Google, and Microsoft on accuracy. That precision comes at a cost, though. items.title: Google Deepmind shifts genomics AI from bulk tissue predictions to single cell type resolution with AlphaGenome 2
items.summary: Google Deepmind has unveiled AlphaGenome 2, an AI model that analyzes genetic variants for individual cell types rather than across bulk tissue. Trained on more than 107 million cell profiles, it identifies nearly twice as many disease-relevant gene changes as its predecessor. items.title: Australia's proposed AI safety bill would force frontier model makers to open up to independent testing
items.summary: Australia's government, led by Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, wants to enshrine mandatory safety rules for frontier AI companies in law for the first time. A new regulator would enforce independent model audits and impose steep penalties for violations. items.title: Google joins the decision-model wave with Gemini Decision 1, scoring 1,000 questions in a single pass
items.summary: Google Deepmind's new Gemini Decisions API evaluates up to 1,000 closed-ended questions in a single pass across text, images, audio, and video. Gemini Decision 1 returns results in 150 to 250 milliseconds at roughly five times lower cost than Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite, according to Google. The article Google joins the decision-model wave with Gemini Decision 1, scoring 1,000 questions in a single pass appeared first on The Decoder.

items.title: US corporate AI spending hits a new high in October, but growth slows to 1.65 percent
items.summary: According to the Ramp AI Index, US corporate AI spending rose just 1.65 percent in October 2026. One percent of companies still drive 80 percent of revenue for OpenAI and Anthropic. Customer support is emerging as a new growth driver, but it may bring lower margins than the coding business that has fueled spending so far. The article US corporate AI spending hits a new high in October, but growth slows to 1.65 percent appeared first on The Decode

items.title: Google Deepmind's AlphaProof Code verified Signal's cryptographic core in four weeks instead of years
items.summary: Google Deepmind's AlphaProof Code mathematically verified Signal's cryptographic core code in four weeks, a process that typically takes years. AI agents powered by Gemini Carbon wrote more than six million lines of proof code and flagged only about one percent for human review.
